data.name: Ilona
data.gender_notes: Ilona is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hungarian 'Ilona', which translates to 'God's answer' or 'tender one'. The name Ilona carries the meaning “God's answer” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ilona usually hope their child will grow to embody god's answer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes God's answer to prayers and a tender, loving spirit.
data.etymology: Ilona belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's answer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ilona total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: אילונה
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא אור (Elokim hu or) - God is my light
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אילונה נגזר מהמילה העברית 'אלוהים' (אלוהים - Elokim, שם אלוהות) ומ-'אור' (אור - or, שמש), ומשמעותו 'אלוהים הוא אור' או 'אור האל'. השם מופיע במספר מקורות יהודיים ומשקף את הקשר בין אלוהים לאור הרוחני.

in_greek.name: Ιλόνα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιλόνα πιθανόν να προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'ήλιος' (Helios), που σημαίνει 'Ήλιος' ή 'όμορφο φως'. Σε χριστιανικό πλαίσιο, μπορεί να συμβολίζει το φως του Θεού ή το πνεύμα του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Ilona
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Ilona is derived from the Hungarian and Finnish languages, suggesting a connection to the concept of light or beauty. In Christian tradition, it may symbolize spiritual illumination or inner beauty.

in_english.name: Ilona
in_english.meaning: God is my light or beautiful shining one
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ilona has multifaceted origins, with possible roots in Hebrew (אלוהים הוא אור - Elokim hu or) and Greek (Ήλιος - Helios). It symbolizes spiritual light, divine illumination, and inner beauty. While not directly mentioned in the Bible, the name resonates with biblical themes of light and divine presence. Historically, Ilona has been used in various Christian cultures, representing a connection to faith and spirituality.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ilona has been popular in Hungarian culture for centuries, with several notable figures holding this name. It evokes a sense of strength and determination, reflecting the resilient spirit of the Hungarian people.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ilona holds deep spiritual significance, implying a strong connection to God. It reminds us that God is the answer to our prayers and the source of our tenderness and love. Wearing this name is a constant affirmation of faith and a reminder to seek God's guidance and grace in all aspects of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ilona, meaning "goddess of grace and beauty," is a name that embodies the divine feminine. It is a reminder of the inherent dignity and worth of all women, and a call to honor the beauty and grace present in the world around us.

historical_references.context: Ilona was the eldest daughter of King Béla IV of Hungary. She was married to King Ottokar II of Bohemia in 1235. Ilona died in childbirth in 1241.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Ilona remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.
